sources.citation: WALS Online (CLDF, local copy: language 'oku' (source Davis-1992)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Only features 10A/10B (vowel nasalization) coded for Oku; no stress (14A-17A) or tone (13A) datapoints.

sources.citation: Davis, Leslie Kim. 1992. A Segmental Phonology of the Oku Language. M.A. thesis, University of Texas at Arlington. xi+109 pp. (SIL Language & Culture Archives item 9762)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: online with a university library login
sources.note: Nothing. Whole thesis scanned and searched; TOC has no stress/accent/prosody section (ch.2 noun classes, syllable structure, word structure, segmental phonemes; ch.3 processes; ch.4 interpretation). p.14: 'This study will not deal with tone in any depth'; tone is mentioned only as evidence for vowel sequences (pp.46-47, 89-90). No use of the words stress/accent/prominence anywhere.

sources.citation: Blood, Cynthia L. 1999. The Oku noun class system. Yaoundé: SIL / Ministry of Scientific and Technical Research. 25 pp. (SIL archive item 32320)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Gives tone-marking conventions (low, high, mid, high-falling, mid-falling, low-falling) and prefix tone analysis after Davis; noun-class morphology only.

sources.citation: Nforbi, Emmanuel (1993). Oku Verb Morphology: Tense Aspects and Mood. Université de Yaoundé. Université de Yaoundé I. xii+92 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Language is not in the catalog and has no existing stress statements. The work says nothing about word stress; it only confirms the tonal analysis already recorded for Oku in this reading folder (Davis 1992/1997, Blood 1999, Hyman 2014). The open copy was re-downloaded once from pure.mpg.

sources.citation: Davis, Leslie. 1997. Tone in the Oku noun and verb. Yaoundé: SIL / Ministry of Scientific and Technical Research. 19 pp. (SIL archive item 47909)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Describes surface tone melodies of CVC/CVV nouns and verbs in isolation and in frames, underlying melodies, floating/grammatical H tones, contour restrictions per syllable/TBU; CVV treated as bisyllabic (fn.4 citing Davis 1992:89-90).
Nothing; consonant/vowel inventory and alphabet only; cites Davis 1992, Blood & Davis 1999, Nforbi 1993, Ethnologue.

sources.citation: Hyman, Larry M. 2014. How to study a tone language, with exemplification from Oku (Grassfields Bantu, Cameroon). Language Documentation & Conservation 8: 525-562. hdl:10125/24624 (earlier version: UC Berkeley PhonLab Annual Report 2010, doi:10.5070/P72TR4S97H)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing about stress in Oku (the only 'stress' mentions concern Corejuage in the appendix). Full tonal analysis of Oku from 1977 fieldnotes: surface H, M, L, L˚ before pause, falling contours HM/HL/ML, no rising contours; nouns mostly prefix+monosyllabic root with M (occasionally L, never H) prefixes; underlying /H/ vs /L/ with M derived (p.545-546).

sources.citation: Blood, Cynthia L. & Leslie Davis. 1999. Oku-English provisional lexicon. Yaoundé: SIL. (SIL archive item 47878)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Introduction explains numeric tone-pattern codes (1=high, 3=high falling, 5=mid, 6=mid falling, 7=low, 8=low falling) per entry; no prosodic prominence discussed.

sources.citation: Yensi, Agnes Mbibeh. 1996. The noun class system of Oku. Maîtrise thesis, Université de Yaoundé. xi+134 pp. (MPG PuRe item_403559; hdl:11858/00-001M-0000-0012-801B-6)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. §1.7 'The sound system of Oku' (vowels, consonants, syllable types of affixes, brief tone remarks: nasals can bear tone); no stress/accent statement.

sources.citation: Nforbi, Emmanuel. 1993. Oku verb morphology: tense, aspect and mood. Postgraduate (Maîtrise) thesis, Université de Yaoundé. xii+92 pp. (MPG PuRe item_403557; hdl:11858/00-001M-0000-0012-8017-E)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. §1.7 'Aspects of Phonology' (pp.14-18) reproduces Davis's inventories and syllable types and adds §1.7.6 'The Tone System': 'We identified four tones in Oku: high, low, mid, and falling', with minimal pairs; tone also grammatical (floating H marks progressive etc.).
